uncited: This method defines the memory layout and access patterns for dense voxel volumes, storing data in a single contiguous 1D array mapped from 3D coordinates.
It solves the problem of efficient spatial indexing and boundary validation in GPU or CPU-based volume rendering by replacing multi-dimensional array overhead with linear memory access.

It differs from brick-based approaches [8114-voxel-renderer-with-top-level-grid-and-bricks.md] by using a flat grid, and from material packing [4907-voxel-material-packing.md] by focusing on raw data storage rather than attribute compression.
If invalid, handle error or return default value.

- Coordinate order must match the layout assumption (C-order: X fastest, Z slowest) [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the coordinate order matches the layout assumption of C-order (X fastest, Z slowest). The evidence explicitly states that the system uses (Z, Y, X) layout to 'align with NumPy C-order contiguity'. In C-order (row-major) storage, the last index varies fastest. Therefore, in a (Z, Y, X) tuple, X is the last index and thus the fastest-varying dimension, while Z is the first index and thus the slowest-varying dimension. This directly supports the claim that X is fastest and Z is slowest in this C-order layout.
